applicability.rationale: Participants were individually randomized 1:1 to parallel botulinum toxin A or placebo groups using a centralized schedule.

results.relation_rationale: The selected primary outcome matches the requested weekly self-reported pain-intensity change from baseline versus placebo over 24 weeks after the first administration.

reported.analysis_population: Intention-to-treat population: 34 participants assigned to botulinum toxin A and 32 assigned to placebo; primary outcome analyses used last-observation-carried-forward imputation for missing values.

endpoint.name: self-reported mean pain intensity over 24 weeks

results.requested_outcome: Change from baseline in self-reported mean weekly pain intensity over 24 weeks

comparison_groups.assignment: Two successive subcutaneous administrations of botulinum toxin A (up to 300 units), 12 weeks apart.
Two successive subcutaneous placebo administrations, 12 weeks apart.

target.intended_analysis_population: All randomized participants in the comparison groups
target.intended_effect_measure: Between-group difference in mean change from baseline

measurement.method: Daily pain diary: mean pain over the past 24 hours recorded each morning on the Brief Pain Inventory 0–10 numerical rating scale; weekly mean.
measurement.metric: Change from baseline in self-reported mean weekly pain intensity over 24 weeks

target.outcome_definition: Change from baseline in self-reported mean weekly pain intensity over 24 weeks

time_point_or_window.description: From baseline (one week before randomization) over 24 weeks after the first administration
